title: Checkboxes or Radios?
prompt:
Choice controls have rules. Build both kinds:

- A group of three `radio` inputs named `size` (values `s`, `m`, `l`) — radios share a `name`, so only one can be picked.
- A single `checkbox` named `gift` (value `yes`) — independent on/off.
- A `label` for each control, wired with `for`/`id`.

Rules:
- All three radios share `name="size"`.
- The checkbox uses `name="gift"`.
- Every control has a connected label.
boilerplate: Choose a size

tests.name: three radios sharing one name
tests.hint: Radios in the same group all carry the same name="size"; give each a different value.

tests.name: radio values s, m, l
tests.hint: value="s", value="m", value="l" — one per radio.

tests.name: one independent checkbox
tests.hint: <input type="checkbox" name="gift" value="yes"> — on/off, independent of the radios.

tests.name: every control has a wired label
tests.hint: One <label for="…"> per control — radios and checkbox all need one.
